title: A rational lift extends to a section on a locally closed subscheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a point $x\in X$, the following are equivalent: (i) there is $y\in Y$ with $f(y)=x$ and induced map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]; (ii) there is a locally closed subscheme $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ containing $x$ and a morphism $s:Z\to Y$ with $f\circ s=j$. Here a locally closed subscheme means an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and containing $x$ means $x\in j(Z)$. No quasi-compactness or separation assumption is imposed on $Y$ or $f$.

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.3, printed p. 27 (cd(f) and sections over subschemes); its proof chooses an open of the reduced closure of x.

proof.text: Assume (i), and write $r:\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(y)$ for its residue-field map. Put $K=\kappa(x)$. The canonical field-valued point $j_y$ and naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field, lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] give $t=j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r^{-1}):\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ with $f\circ t=j_x$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ about $x$ and, using the affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$ about $y$, with $B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra. A map from a one-point field spectrum whose image lies in an open factors through that open: restrict the map to the inverse image, which is the whole source [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $t$ factors through $V$. Under the affine correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum], write $\alpha:A\to B$ for $f|_V$ and $\psi:B\to K$ for this factorization. Identify $x$ with a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Open-immersion residue invariance and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] identify $K$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $f\circ t=j_x$ gives $\psi\alpha=\pi:A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.3, printed p. 27 (cd(f) and sections over subschemes); its proof chooses an open of the reduced closure of x.

proof.text:
Set $R=A/\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra], $R$ embeds into $K$ and $K$ is its fraction field. Choose $A$-algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $B$, and write $\psi(b_i)=u_i/v_i$ with $u_i,v_i\in R$ and $v_i
e0$. Set $d=\prod_i v_i
e0$, taking $d=1$ if $m=0$, and $D=R[1/d]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The fraction map $\iota:D	o K$, $u/d^q\mapsto u/d^q$, is injective: equality in $K$ gives equality of cross-products in the domain $R$, hence equality in $D$. Each $u_i/v_i=u_i\prod_{h
e i}v_h/d$ belongs to its image. Since every element of $B$ is a polynomial in the $b_i$ with coefficients from $A$, all of $\psi(B)$ lies in $\iota(D)$. Define $ eta:B	o D$ as $\iota^{-1}\psi$ on this image. Injectivity of $\iota$ makes $ eta$ a ring map and gives $ eta\alpha=\lambda:A	o A/\mathfrak p	o D$. This is an explicit finite-generator calculation; no finite presentation, relation-lifting, or separation assertion is used.

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.3, printed p. 27 (cd(f) and sections over subschemes); its proof chooses an open of the reduced closure of x.

proof.text: Choose $a\in A$ lifting $d\in R$, so $a\notin\mathfrak p$. Put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$. The map $\lambda:A\to D$ factors as $A\to A[1/a]\xrightarrow{q}D$, where $q(c/a^e)=\bar c/d^e$. This formula respects the fraction equivalence of [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $q$ is surjective because every $u/d^e$ has a numerator lifted from $A$. Since $q$ is surjective, it induces a ring isomorphism $A[1/a]/\ker q\cong D$, so $\operatorname{Spec}q$ is this isomorphism of spectra followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/a]/\ker q)\to\operatorname{Spec}A[1/a]$, which is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]; precomposing with an isomorphism keeps both conditions of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Therefore $\operatorname{Spec}q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A[1/a]$ is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/a]\to U$ is an open immersion. Its composite with $U\to X$ is an open immersion, since the composite of two isomorphisms onto open subschemes is again one [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $j:Z\to X$ induced by $\lambda$ is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, hence an immersion. This is precisely an affine open of the reduced closure of $x$ used in ILO II 2.2.3; the construction does not assume that the singleton $\{x\}$ is locally closed.

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.3, printed p. 27 (cd(f) and sections over subschemes); its proof chooses an open of the reduced closure of x.

proof.text: Define $s:Z\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\beta}V\hookrightarrow Y$. Contravariant functoriality and the equality $\beta\alpha=\lambda$ from Step 2 give $f\circ s=j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Also $\iota\lambda=\pi$; applying $\operatorname{Spec}$ shows that the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\iota}Z\xrightarrow{j}X$ is $j_x$, using the canonical affine residue-field identification from Step 1 [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification]. Since $j_x$ maps the unique point to $x$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $x$ lies in $j(Z)$. This proves (ii).

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.3, printed p. 27 (cd(f) and sections over subschemes); its proof chooses an open of the reduced closure of x.

proof.text: Conversely assume (ii), choose $z\in Z$ with $j(z)=x$, and set $y=s(z)$. Then $f(y)=x$. Factor the immersion $j$ as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The closed-immersion residue-field isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso] and the open-immersion assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] show that the induced map $c:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism. By the residue-field maps of [def-weil-residue-field], $f\circ s=j$ gives $ba=c$, where $a:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ and $b:\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$. Put $b'=c^{-1}b$, so $b'a=1$. A unital homomorphism of fields is injective: its kernel is a proper ideal of a field, hence zero. Consequently, for $v\in\kappa(y)$, $b'(a(b'(v)))=b'(v)$ implies $a(b'(v))=v$. Thus $ab'=1$ as well, so $a$ is an isomorphism, proving (i). No quasi-compactness or separatedness of $Y$ is used in either direction.
